Chapter 10: Creating a Life of Radical Hospitality
You know, there’s something truly powerful about being welcomed—about walking into a room and feeling like you’re seen, valued, and right where you belong. We all crave that sense of belonging, don’t we? But honestly, not many of us know how to create it for others.
The thing is, radical hospitality isn’t about throwing fancy dinners or having the perfect home. It’s really about making space for people, just as they are.
Let me share a story. There was this couple who opened their home to a group of college students one Thanksgiving. None of the students had anywhere to go. The house? It was small. The food? Super simple. But the laughter and stories? They filled every single corner. One student, who’d been feeling lost and far from family, later said it was the first time in months he truly felt at home. And that’s when it hits you: hospitality isn’t about impressing—it’s about including.
Most of us fall into the habit of waiting for an invitation, hoping someone else will take the first step. But here’s the thing—love takes initiative. It looks for people who are on the edges, folks who feel left out, and says, “Hey, you belong here.”
There’s another story I love. A single dad started hosting Sunday dinners for his neighbors, inviting anyone who wanted to join. At first, only a couple of people showed up. But week after week, that table grew—and so did the sense of community. People brought their own dishes, their stories, even their struggles. Those dinners became a lifeline. It was a place where everyone was welcome, no matter what.
Radical hospitality is about opening your life, not just your home. It’s about noticing who isn’t there, reaching out, and making space for them. Most folks don’t realize how much a simple invitation can mean. But over time, these small acts of welcome—they add up. They create a real culture of belonging, where everyone finds a place.
